posts.content_md:
Hi everyone, it's me again!

I've got a bit of a problem figuring out the pixel size of the CCD I'm using. It's a Moticam 2000 2m pixel Camera (1600*1200). 

I went through quite a lot of websites, none of them has the information. Could anyone give me a hand?

En...also, Marry Christmas and Happy New Year guys!!!

Cheers,

ztp

posts.author: holo_cyware
posts.content_md:
Well, from the specs we learn that this camera has a 1/2 inch CCD.

Now, the CCD's tend to be the same in the same technology "limits"; we can find at least the size of the pixel for a "certain" 1/2 inch CCD 1200x1600, like here: [http://viewbits.com/2-megapixel-CMOS-camera.html](http://viewbits.com/2-megapixel-CMOS-camera.html)

I'd say that the physical size of a pixel on the senzor must be in the 4x4 microns range (the pixels are square; this particular camera that I have found has 4.2x4.2 microns)

posts.author: ztp911
posts.content_md:
Thanks man!

I actually assumed that the pixel is 4.2 * 4.2 microns after some trials and errors! Since 4.2 gives me the best image quality.

Another question: How do I tell if this camera is 8-bit or 10-bit? I was told that images taken by a 10-bit camera need to be converted into 8-bit. If it is the case, how do I go about converting the images?

Finally, the holograms I've taken are all 1600*1200. To be able to use FFT later on, I cropped them to 1024*1024, just wondering if the cropping causes some loss of data?

You help is much appreciated!

Cheers~

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Cropping will restrict the view points. Imagine taping off the sides of a window into a scene. So yes you do lose data.
